findings.claim: In concatenatedRSToASN1DER, lines 114-115 call ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger) and ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger) and discard the results. The return statement at lines 117-121 repeats the encoding with new encoders, so lines 114-115 are dead code.

verifier.reason: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:114-115 create two fresh ASN1Encoder instances, write r and s into their private ByteArrayOutputStreams and discard them; ASN1Encoder.create()/write (ASN1Encoder.java:42-49) have no shared state or side effects, and the return at lines 117-121 re-encodes with new encoders, so the two statements are dead.

findings.claim: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider() no longer throws the fail-fast 'Multiple crypto providers loaded' IllegalStateException; it picks the highest order() instead. The Default, Elytron and FIPS1402 providers all return 200, so a tie is decided by ServiceLoader/classpath order. For example, a FIPS deployment with a stray crypto-default jar can run on non-FIPS BouncyCastle without failing.

verifier.reason: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:56-71 now sorts by order() descending and returns the first provider, with the 'Multiple crypto providers loaded' exception removed; DefaultCryptoProvider.java:83, WildFlyElytronProvider.java:76 and FIPS1402Provider.java:114 all return 200, so the stable sort leaves ties in ServiceLoader order. The FIPS example holds only for auto-detect callers of init() (e.g. Globals.java:44, KeycloakApplication.java:89, AuthzClient.java:95); the Quarkus server sets the provider explicitly from FipsMode at KeycloakRecorder.java:210-215, so it is not affected.

findings.claim: int order() is added to the public CryptoProvider SPI interface as an abstract method with no default. External implementations stop compiling, and already-compiled ones throw AbstractMethodError when the detectProvider comparator calls order().

verifier.reason: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:44 declares `int order();` with no default, and CryptoIntegration.java:57 sorts ServiceLoader-discovered providers with `Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order)`, so an external implementation no longer compiles. A pre-compiled one would throw AbstractMethodError only when two or more providers are on the classpath (a single-element sort never calls the comparator); all four in-repo implementations are updated.

findings.claim: Crypto is initialized with AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader() instead of the thread context class loader. CryptoProvider implementations visible only through the context class loader can be missed, and the wrong provider may be selected.

verifier.reason: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/AuthzClient.java:95 calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()), and common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:56 runs ServiceLoader only against that loader, so a higher-order provider visible only via the context class loader would be skipped in favour of the limited AuthzClientCryptoProvider. This only matters in split-classloader deployments, matches the existing convention at services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/KeycloakApplication.java:89, and init is a no-op if the application has already initialised crypto.

findings.claim: AuthzClient.create now calls CryptoIntegration.init, which sets JVM-global first-caller-wins crypto state. If only the stub provider is visible, it stays pinned for the JVM, and most of its methods throw UnsupportedOperationException.

verifier.reason: AuthzClient.create now calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()) (authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/AuthzClient.java:95), and init only assigns the static cryptoProvider when it is null (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:30-33), so a later init with a different class loader cannot replace the stub; only an explicit setProvider (CryptoIntegration.java:96) can. AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException from 16 of its 20 methods, e.g. getAlgorithmProvider, getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getSignature (authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:74-224).

findings.claim: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the provider of the default KeyStore type (e.g. SUN for JKS), not a BouncyCastle provider. As a result, BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER is derived incorrectly.

verifier.reason: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:61-67 returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, a JDK provider rather than BouncyCastle, so `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/util/BouncyIntegration.java:34-39) takes that provider's name whenever this provider is selected. The effect is harmless: with this provider active, the only reader of `PROVIDER` is a debug log at common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:34, and the BC-backed providers (order 200) outrank it (order 100) when present.

findings.claim: For indefinite-length encoding (0x80), ASN1Decoder.readLength() returns -1, and callers do not handle it. readSequence skips its loop or computes length arithmetic on -1, and readInteger calls read(-1), which throws NegativeArraySizeException instead of IOException.

verifier.reason: `readLength()` returns -1 for 0x80 (ASN1Decoder.java:133-135) and no caller checks it: `readSequence` skips its `while (length > 0)` loop and returns an empty list (:55-62), `readNext` does `length += reset()` on -1 (:80-82), and `readInteger` passes it to `read(length)` where `new byte[-1]` throws NegativeArraySizeException (:71-72, :170). Through the only production caller (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:128-134) a 0x80 length surfaces as an IOException instead, so the unchecked exception needs a direct `readInteger` call on such input.

findings.claim: The DER decoder implements general-purpose high-tag-number and indefinite-length decoding. DER ECDSA signatures only need a 0x30 SEQUENCE containing two 0x02 INTEGERs.

verifier.reason: The new authz/client/.../util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java has a general high-tag-number loop (lines 93-125) and an indefinite-length branch returning -1 (lines 133-135), yet its only caller is asn1derToConcatenatedRS in AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:128-134, which reads one SEQUENCE of two INTEGERs. The indefinite-length part is only recognised, not actually decoded: no caller handles the -1, so the claim overstates that half, but the unneeded generality is real.

findings.claim: In DER parsing, a zero-length INTEGER throws NumberFormatException instead of being handled as a parse error.

verifier.reason: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:71-73, `readInteger()` passes a length of 0 straight to `read(0)` and then `new BigInteger(new byte[0])`, which throws the unchecked NumberFormatException ("Zero length BigInteger") rather than the method's declared IOException. The only in-repo caller of the conversion, core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/crypto/ECDSASignatureSignerContext.java:33-35, catches `Exception` and feeds it DER produced by the local JCA signer, so the bad input is not realistically reachable there.

findings.claim: No upgrade/migration or release note is provided for the breaking CryptoProvider SPI change, although PR-CHECKLIST.md requires one.

verifier.reason: The patch adds an abstract `int order()` with no default to the ServiceLoader-loaded interface at common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:44, which breaks any out-of-tree implementation, yet it touches no docs file and no .adoc in the repo mentions CryptoProvider. PR-CHECKLIST.md:9 asks for release-note and upgrade-guide updates only "if applicable" and allows them in an associated PR, so the requirement is conditional and this is a documentation gap for an undocumented internal interface.

findings.claim: The ES256, ES384 and ES512 tests in ECDSAAlgorithmTest all use one key from the default-curve KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC"). Curve-appropriate key sizes (P-384, P-521) and the DER long-form length paths (length > 127 in ASN1Encoder.writeLength / ASN1Decoder.readLength) are therefore never exercised.

verifier.reason: authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:42 generates one key with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() (JDK default curve, P-256 or P-384) and reuses it for ES256/ES384/ES512 at lines 59-72. With r and s at most 49 bytes the DER sequence body is at most 102 bytes, so the length > 127 branches at ASN1Encoder.java:67 and ASN1Decoder.java:137 are never reached; only a P-521 key (body up to ~136 bytes) would hit them, and no other test in authz/client uses these classes.

findings.claim: No test covers the new order()-based provider selection logic in CryptoIntegration.

verifier.reason: The only test the patch adds, authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java, instantiates AuthzClientCryptoProvider directly and exercises only ECDSA encoding. No test in the repository references order() or checks which provider wins when several are found by the new sort at common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 (common/src/test has no CryptoIntegration test).

findings.claim: detectProvider instantiates every CryptoProvider via ServiceLoader, so constructor side effects of non-selected providers still occur. For example, the FIPS provider inserts Security providers even when it is not selected.

verifier.reason: `detectProvider` collects every ServiceLoader-instantiated `CryptoProvider` into a list before picking index 0 (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:56-58,71), and the `FIPS1402Provider` constructor calls `Security.insertProviderAt` unconditionally (crypto/fips1402/src/main/java/org/keycloak/crypto/fips/FIPS1402Provider.java:94-98). The patch replaced the old "multiple providers" exception with silently ignoring the rest, so a non-selected FIPS provider (possible only when it ties at order 200 with the default or Elytron provider) still mutates the JVM security provider list.

findings.claim: The ignored-providers debug line passes a runtime-built string as the debugf format string, so a '%' in it would be misinterpreted.

verifier.reason: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:69 calls logger.debugf(builder.toString()), where the string is built at runtime from provider class names (lines 65-68) and used as the printf format. The only variable content is class names, which in practice never contain '%', so this is a style nit (should be debug(...) or debugf("%s", ...)).

findings.claim: The ignored-providers debug message leaves a trailing ', ' in its output.

verifier.reason: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:66-69 appends `getClass().getName() + ", "` for every ignored provider and logs `builder.toString()` without trimming, so the debug message always ends with a trailing ", ".

findings.claim: concatenatedRSToASN1DER() assumes signature.length == signLength without validating it. A malformed signature can throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException.

verifier.reason: The new authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:103-110 does System.arraycopy(signature, 0, r, 1, len) and System.arraycopy(signature, len, s, 1, len) with no check that signature.length == signLength, so a short signature throws an unchecked index-out-of-bounds exception rather than IOException (and a long one is silently truncated). The practical effect is small: it mirrors the existing BCECDSACryptoProvider.java:28-35, and the caller at core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/crypto/ECDSASignatureVerifierContext.java:32 catches Exception and wraps it in VerificationException.

findings.claim: The ECDSA tests only check a self round-trip, comparing rsConcat to rsConcat2. The DER output is never verified independently (e.g. with Signature.verify), so a symmetric encoder/decoder bug would pass.

verifier.reason: authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:53-56 decodes a JCA signature, re-encodes it, decodes again and asserts only rsConcat == rsConcat2. The re-encoded DER (asn1Des) is never compared to the original `sign` nor checked with Signature.verify, so an encoder bug the lenient decoder tolerates would pass.

findings.claim: DER parsing ignores trailing bytes after the parsed structure.

verifier.reason: `ASN1Decoder.readSequence()` (authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:49-63) returns once the declared sequence length is consumed and never checks that the stream is exhausted, so `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:125) silently accepts trailing bytes. The only caller is ECDSASignatureSignerContext.java:33, which feeds it the locally produced JCA signature, so the input is not attacker-controlled.

findings.claim: ASN1Decoder tag checks mask the tag with 0x1f, ignoring the class and constructed bits.

verifier.reason: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:94 computes `tagNo = tag & 0x1f`, and readSequence (line 52) and readInteger (line 68) compare only that number to ASN1Encoder.SEQUENCE (0x10) / INTEGER (0x02), so class bits and the constructed bit (0x20) are never checked — e.g. 0x10, 0x30, 0x90 all pass as a SEQUENCE and 0x02, 0x22, 0x82 as an INTEGER.
